promise_band.headline: We clean up like we were never here
promise_band.body: It is the thing our customers mention most. Forms out, debris hauled, the site swept, and a walk-through with you before the trucks leave. Concrete work is messy while it is happening. It should not still be messy the next morning.

process_steps.headline: How a project runs with us

steps.title: You call, we come measure
steps.body: Nick or Connor comes out, measures the area and talks through what you want. Customers regularly get their quote back the same day they called.

steps.title: We handle the permit
steps.body: If your drive ties into a public street, or your county wants a patio approval, our permitting manager files it and follows it through. You do not chase it.

steps.title: Tear-out and base prep
steps.body: The old slab comes out and the subgrade gets rebuilt and compacted. This is the step that decides whether the concrete is still flat in ten years.

steps.title: Pour, finish, joint
steps.body: We pour, finish to the texture you chose, and cut control joints so the slab cracks where we put the line instead of across the middle.

steps.title: Clean up and walk through
steps.body: Site cleared and swept, then we walk it with you. We tell you how long to stay off it and when it is ready for vehicles.

seo_body.headline: Why Indiana concrete fails early — and what we do about it
paragraphs: Central Indiana runs through dozens of freeze-thaw cycles a year. Water gets into the slab, freezes, expands, and prises the concrete apart from the inside. That is why a driveway here can look fine at eighteen months and be spalling at three years. The weather is not the variable you can change — the base, the mix, the joints and the sealer are.

So we spend the time underneath the slab. The subgrade gets excavated and compacted properly rather than skimmed and poured over, because a slab bridging a soft spot will crack no matter how good the finish looks on day one. We cut control joints at the right spacing and depth so the inevitable movement shows up as a straight line in a joint instead of a jagged crack across the middle of your driveway.

Sealing is the other half. A penetrating sealer keeps water and de-icing salt out of the surface, and it is far cheaper to reseal a good slab every few years than to replace a bad one once. We will tell you honestly whether your existing concrete is worth sealing or whether you would be throwing money at something already past saving.
checklist: Excavated and compacted subgrade, not a skim-and-pour
Control joints cut to depth and spacing
Finishes chosen for grip as well as looks
Sealing quoted separately so you can see what it costs

faqs.q: How long does a concrete driveway take?
faqs.a: Most residential driveways are a one-day job — tear-out, base prep and pour all happen the same day. Larger or multi-stage projects run longer, and your estimator will tell you which one yours is before you book.

faqs.q: When can I drive on new concrete?
faqs.a: Stay off it on foot for at least 24 hours. Vehicles should wait about 7 days, and heavy vehicles longer. Concrete keeps gaining strength for around 28 days, so avoid parking anything heavy near the edges in that first month.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit, and who gets it?
faqs.a: Often yes. Indianapolis requires a driveway permit for any drive connecting to a city street, and Hendricks County and the Town of Plainfield have their own approvals for drives and patios. We have a permitting manager on staff who files and follows these for you.

All concrete moves, and control joints exist so it cracks along a line we chose rather than across the middle. What we can prevent is the structural cracking that comes from a poor base — which is why the excavation and compaction step matters more than the finish.

faqs.q: Do you do commercial work as well as residential?
faqs.a: Yes. We handle both. Alongside flatwork we take on hardscaping, culvert replacement, drainage installation and asphalt paving.

faqs.q: How much does a driveway cost around Indianapolis?
faqs.a: It depends on square footage, how much tear-out there is, access for the trucks, thickness, reinforcement and finish. That is why we measure on site rather than quoting over the phone. The estimate is free and there is no obligation.

In central Indiana it is usually worth it. A penetrating sealer keeps water and road salt out of the surface, which is what causes spalling after a few winters. We will tell you if your existing slab is too far gone to be worth sealing.

We are based in Plainfield and work across the Indianapolis metro — Indianapolis, Avon, Brownsburg, Carmel, Fishers and the surrounding towns, plus outlying areas including Greenwood, Westfield, Noblesville, Mooresville and Bloomington.
